# What the data-dict export loses: Cooperative Election Study (CES)

The YAML files here follow data-dict spec 0.1.0. They describe the common data format, so they validate against its parquet files. The records in `metadata/` remain canonical. This table counts what the export drops or flattens into text.

| | `cumulative` | `2020` | `2022` | `2024` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| variables exported | 22 | 18 | 18 | 18 |
| variables whose numeric code labels went to `details` (no labeled numeric codes) | 17 | 15 | 15 | 15 |
| missing or unresolved codes, typed only in the `__code` column's labels | 25 | 49 | 48 | 47 |
| variables listed by name only (no type the records can support) | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| availability entries (wave by form, with n), summarized as one line of text | 387 | 18 | 18 | 18 |
| field origins (publisher, data file, rule, hand, model) not exported | 167 | 123 | 123 | 124 |
| links between releases, not exported | 86 | 86 | 86 | 86 |
| release id not expressible as data-dict `version` (needs semver or a date) | 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 |
